en Keller was a great humanitarian
. She cared deeply for the sick. Injured and
disabled people. The disabled people have physical or mental problems that limit their
activities or senses. Helen devoted her life to help them.
cn was born in 1880 in Alabama, USA. Her parents were Captain Arthur Keller and
Katherine Adams Keller.
Her family was not rich. Their main source of income was
ton plantation.
en was born healthy, but in 1882 she became deaf, dumb and blind after a high
er. Her father heard about Perkins Sc
ool for the Blind in Boston and contacted the
Director there. In 1887, the Director sent one of his best students, Anne Sullivan, to
p Helen. Anne worked hard to enable
her to communicate.
1890, Helen's formal education started at Horace Mann School for the deaf in
Boston. In 1892, she went to Wright Humason School for the deaf in New York. Helen
improved her communication skills an
studied regular academic subjects. She then
to go to college, and attended Cambridge School for Young Ladies in 1896.
Later, she studied at Radcliffe College. Here she learnt Braille, which was a new
technique for reading. She also learnt how to type. Anne Sullivan was always with
Helen. She sat with Helen in class and hi
elped her by interpreting lectures and texts. In
1904, Helen received her BA degree witl
h Honours from Radcliffe College.
Helen spent her life helping disabled people to leai.11. She died on June 1, 1968.
(a) Who helped Helen Keller communicate after she lost her senses?
A school teacher
(b) What was Helen Keller’s family’s primary source of income?

en Keller was a great humanitarian
. She cared deeply for the sick. Injured and
disabled people. The disabled people have physical or mental problems that limit their
activities or senses. Helen devoted her life to help them.
cn was born in 1880 in Alabama, USA. Her parents were Captain Arthur Keller and
Katherine Adams Keller.
Her family was not rich. Their main source of income was
ton plantation.
en was born healthy, but in 1882 she became deaf, dumb and blind after a high
er. Her father heard about Perkins Sc
ool for the Blind in Boston and contacted the
Director there. In 1887, the Director sent one of his best students, Anne Sullivan, to
p Helen. Anne worked hard to enable
her to communicate.
1890, Helen's formal education started at Horace Mann School for the deaf in
Boston. In 1892, she went to Wright Humason School for the deaf in New York. Helen
improved her communication skills an
studied regular academic subjects. She then
to go to college, and attended Cambridge School for Young Ladies in 1896.
Later, she studied at Radcliffe College. Here she learnt Braille, which was a new
technique for reading. She also learnt how to type. Anne Sullivan was always with
Helen. She sat with Helen in class and hi
elped her by interpreting lectures and texts. In
1904, Helen received her BA degree witl
h Honours from Radcliffe College.
Helen spent her life helping disabled people to leai.11. She died on June 1, 1968.

i. Her parents
ii. Anne Sullivan
iii. A doctor
iv. A school teacher
(b) What was Helen Keller’s family’s primary source of income?
